1.title: Advanced Hunting, Threat Analytics and Hunting Graphs
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Advanced Hunting, Threat Analytics and Hunting Graphs. It covers the exam area three. Perform threat hunting. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Interpret threat analytics in Microsoft Defender X D R. Create hunting graphs, including blast radius. Analyze relationships between entities by using Sentinel Graph. Create Advanced Hunting queries. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: three. Perform threat hunting (twenty to twenty-five percent). Exam format: one hundred minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official Microsoft S C-two hundred study guide and Microsoft Learn.

1.title: Advanced hunting in Defender XDR
1.text: Advanced hunting in Defender X D R. Advanced hunting is the query-based hunting tool of the Defender portal: Investigation and response, then Hunting, then Advanced hunting.

1.title: Advanced hunting in Defender XDR, continued
1.text: Advanced hunting in Defender X D R. The figure shows this: Advanced hunting service limits and where the data comes from.

1.title: Advanced hunting in Defender XDR, continued
1.text: Advanced hunting in Defender X D R. Data range. thirty days for native Defender data; Sentinel tables follow their analytics-tier retention. Result set. one hundred thousand rows per query. Timeout. ten minutes per query. Result size. sixty-four megabytes. C P U. Allocation by tenant size, refreshed every fifteen minutes; usage shown as Low, Medium, High; a warning appears above ten percent and the query is blocked at one hundred percent until the next cycle. Freshness. Event tables are near real time; entity tables refresh every hour. Keep data longer than thirty days by onboarding a Sentinel workspace and setting the analytics-tier retention, or by streaming through the Defender streaming A P I. Data stored only in the Sentinel data lake is not in advanced hunting; use data lake exploration (Module eighteen).

1.title: Advanced hunting in Defender XDR, continued
1.text: Advanced hunting in Defender X D R. Full read. Global Administrator, Security Administrator, Security Reader, Global Reader. Unified R back. Raw data, then Email and collaboration metadata (read) for email tables; Security data basics (read) for alerts and behaviors. Endpoint tables. Governed by Defender for Endpoint R back and device groups. Query resources report: shows the resource use of queries (last day by default); Security Reader or higher sees all users; states completed, failed, throttled.

1.title: Saving and sharing queries
1.text: Saving and sharing queries. My queries. Private to you. Shared queries. Whole organization; chosen with Save query, then Save as. Community queries. From the Git Hub Azure-Sentinel repository, reviewed before publishing. Share link copies a direct link. Deleting a saved query is permanent. Functions you can call in a query include File Profile() (file prevalence and signer data), Device From I P() (which device had an I P) and Assigned I P Addresses() (I P s of a device at a time). Save a query as a custom detection (Module nine) when it should run on a schedule. Exam tip: thirty days, one hundred thousand rows, ten minutes. For longer history, connect Sentinel and set retention.

1.title: Threat analytics
1.text: Threat analytics. Threat analytics is the threat intelligence feature of Defender X D R: reports on active threat actors, techniques and vulnerabilities, with your exposure and your protection. Dashboard: security.microsoft.com or threatanalytics three. Latest threats. Newest reports with active and resolved alert counts. High-impact threats. Reports with the most active and resolved alerts. Highest exposure threats. Reports with the greatest exposure (vulnerable and misconfigured devices).

1.title: Threat analytics, continued
1.text: Threat analytics. Overview. Charts (related incidents, alerts over time, impacted assets, recommended actions, endpoint exposure) and metadata (aliases, origin, targets, my ter attack techniques). Analyst report. Executive summary, overview, detections and hunting queries, techniques, recommendations, references, change log. Related incidents, Impacted assets. Your incidents and assets tied to the threat. Endpoints exposure, Recommended actions. Vulnerable devices and mitigations (tracked in Secure Score). Indicators (preview). I O Cs updated in real time.

1.title: Threat analytics, continued
1.text: Threat analytics. Report types: Activity (a campaign), Actor (a Microsoft-tracked threat actor), Core threat, Technique (one attack technique), Tool, Vulnerability (a C V E or group), oh sint (preview). Tags: Ransomware, Phishing, Activity group, Vulnerability. License. At least one Defender product; Defender for Endpoint Plan one does not grant access. Roles. Security data basics (read) for reports, incidents and assets; Vulnerability management (read) and Exposure Management (read) for exposure data. Link a rule. A custom detection rule can be linked to a report; its alerts then show under Related incidents. Agent. The Threat Intelligence Briefing Agent shows a banner on the page. Exam tip: Threat analytics tells you whether a threat affects you. Related incidents equals you are already hit. Endpoints exposure equals you could be hit.

1.title: The hunting graph
1.text: The hunting graph. The hunting graph shows entities as nodes (devices, accounts, I P s) and relationships as edges. Open Advanced hunting, then the hunting graph icon or Create new, then Hunting graph. Predefined scenarios. For example Attack paths to critical asset, Entity relationship map, Paths between two entities, Potential data exfiltration by device, Paths to domain admins, Kerberoast paths to critical assets, oh auth applications with privileged access. Run. Choose a scenario and inputs, set filters, select Run scenario.

1.title: The hunting graph, continued
1.text: The hunting graph. Filters. Source node (is critical, is vulnerable, is exposed to the internet), target node (has sensitive data, has a risk score), edge type, edge direction, Show only the shortest paths. Prerequisites. Roles as for advanced hunting, Sentinel data lake onboarding and at least read access in Microsoft Security Exposure Management. Blast radius (Module thirteen) is the same graph engine applied to an incident node.

1.title: Microsoft Sentinel graph
1.text: Microsoft Sentinel graph. Sentinel graph is unified graph analytics. It answers questions such as what is the blast radius of a compromised document. Defender portal. Incident graph with blast radius; hunting graph. Purview. Data risk graph in insider risk management and data security investigations. Custom graphs (preview). Author in a Jupiter notebook (V S Code extension), publish and materialize with a graph job, query with Graph Query Language (G Q L) on the Graphs page. On-demand graph jobs keep the graph for thirty days; scheduled jobs rebuild on their schedule. It is billed by the Sentinel graph meter. Exam tip: Hunting graph equals explore relationships and paths. Blast radius equals from an incident node. Both need the Sentinel data lake.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A hunting query returns an error that it reached a limit. Which quota is possible? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: one hundred thousand rows per query, or the ten minute timeout. Advanced hunting returns up to one hundred thousand rows and times out after ten minutes.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A team needs to hunt over one hundred eighty days of Defender X D R data. Which approach meets the requirement? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Onboard a Sentinel workspace and set the analytics-tier retention. Native data covers thirty days; a Sentinel workspace with analytics retention extends it. Data lake data is not in advanced hunting.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An analyst wants a hunting query to be available to every analyst in the organization. What should the analyst do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Use Save query, Save as, and choose Shared queries. Shared queries are visible to the whole organization; My queries are private.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A new report on a ransomware campaign appears in threat analytics. The sock wants to know which of its devices are vulnerable to the threat. Which tab helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Endpoints exposure, which shows vulnerable devices. Endpoints exposure shows exposure from vulnerabilities and affected devices; Related incidents shows incidents that already exist.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A hunter wants to see paths from internet-exposed vulnerable devices to critical assets. Which tool and scenario fit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The hunting graph, with Attack paths to critical asset. The hunting graph has the predefined scenario Attack paths to critical asset with source filters such as is exposed to the internet.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which license statement about threat analytics is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A license for at least one Defender product is needed, but Defender for Endpoint Plan one does not qualify. Threat analytics needs a license for at least one Defender product; Defender for Endpoint P one does not grant access.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many rows can advanced hunting return? Answer: one hundred thousand per query. Question two. What is the advanced hunting query timeout? Answer: ten minutes. Question three. Which report type describes a Microsoft-tracked threat actor? Answer: Actor.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What language queries a custom Sentinel graph? Answer: Graph Query Language (G Q L). Question five. How long does an on-demand graph job keep its graph? Answer: thirty days. Question six. Which saved query location is private to you? Answer: My queries.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Limits: thirty days, one hundred thousand rows, ten minutes, sixty-four megabytes. Longer history: onboard Sentinel and set analytics retention; lake data is not in advanced hunting. Saved queries: My, Shared (whole org), Community; deleting is permanent. Threat analytics: dashboard sections, report types, exposure tabs; not included with Defender for Endpoint P one. Hunting graph: nodes and edges, predefined scenarios, needs data lake and Exposure Management read. Sentinel graph: blast radius, custom graphs with G Q L, graph jobs.
